paper_a.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (Bahdanau et al., 2014)

paper_b.title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

metadata.description: The Transformer extends Bahdanau attention from an auxiliary mechanism on top of RNNs to the sole computational primitive of the architecture. Bahdanau introduced additive attention over encoder states to solve the fixed-length bottleneck in seq2seq models; the Transformer replaces the RNN backbone entirely with stacked self-attention + cross-attention layers. The core attention operation (weighted sum of values based on query-key compatibility) is preserved but generalized: additive scoring becomes scaled dot-product, single-head becomes multi-head, and cross-attention (encoder-decoder) is augmented by self-attention within each sequence.

matches.explanation: Both define encoder-decoder architectures for sequence-to-sequence tasks. Bahdanau: bidirectional RNN encoder + GRU decoder with attention. Transformer: stacked self-attention encoder + stacked self-attention+cross-attention decoder. Same high-level architecture (encode, attend, decode), fundamentally different building blocks (RNN vs self-attention).

The core attention operation. Bahdanau uses additive attention: $e_{ij} = v_a^\top \tanh(W_a s_{i-1} + U_a h_j)$ followed by softmax and weighted sum. Transformer uses scaled dot-product attention: $\text{softmax}(QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k})V$. Same conceptual operation (compute compatibility scores, normalize, take weighted sum of values), but different scoring function (additive vs multiplicative) and different inputs (RNN states vs projected embeddings).

Bahdanau's attention IS cross-attention: the decoder queries attend to encoder keys/values. The Transformer's cross-attention sub-layer serves the identical function (decoder queries attending to encoder outputs). The Transformer paper explicitly notes this analogy. The key difference: Bahdanau's is single-head additive; Transformer's is multi-head scaled dot-product.

Both interpret attention weights as soft alignment between source and target positions. Bahdanau frames this as 'jointly learning to align and translate'; the Transformer preserves this alignment interpretation in the cross-attention layers.

The bidirectional RNN encoder is specific to Bahdanau. The Transformer replaces it with stacked self-attention layers + positional encoding. The Transformer's self-attention achieves bidirectional context capture without recurrence.
The GRU-based decoder with sequential state updates is specific to Bahdanau. The Transformer's decoder uses masked self-attention + cross-attention + FFN, with no recurrent state.

Both argue that attention solves the long-range dependency / bottleneck problem. Bahdanau: attention eliminates the fixed-length context vector bottleneck of basic encoder-decoder. Transformer: self-attention provides O(1) path length between any two positions vs O(n) for RNNs. Same high-level claim (attention enables long-range information flow), different specific mechanisms and analyses.
Multi-head attention (parallel attention with different projections, concatenated) is a Transformer innovation. Bahdanau uses single-head attention.

Self-attention (Q=K=V from the same sequence) is a Transformer innovation. Bahdanau only uses cross-attention (decoder queries, encoder keys/values). Self-attention is what enables the Transformer to replace the RNN backbone.
Position-wise FFN layers are a Transformer architectural component with no analogue in Bahdanau (which uses the RNN for nonlinear transformation).
Positional encoding (sinusoidal) is needed because the Transformer has no recurrence and thus no inherent notion of position. Bahdanau's RNN naturally encodes position through sequential processing.
Residual connections + layer normalization in the Transformer are architectural design choices not present in Bahdanau's model.

Both evaluate on machine translation. Bahdanau: 36.15 BLEU on WMT'14 En-Fr. Transformer: 41.8 BLEU on the same benchmark (+5.6 BLEU) and 28.4 on En-De. The Transformer dramatically improves upon Bahdanau's results while training much faster.

unmatched_paper_a_explanations.DP_BA.2: Bidirectional RNN encoder. Replaced by self-attention in the Transformer.
unmatched_paper_a_explanations.DP_BA.4: GRU-based decoder with sequential state. Replaced by masked self-attention + cross-attention.

unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_TF.2: Multi-head attention. Novel extension of single-head attention.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_TF.3: Self-attention. Key innovation enabling RNN replacement.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_TF.5: Position-wise FFN. Architectural component replacing RNN nonlinearity.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_TF.6: Positional encoding. Necessary because self-attention is permutation-equivariant.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_TF.8: Residual connections + layer norm. Training stabilization techniques.

summary: The Transformer extends Bahdanau attention from a component layered on top of RNNs to the sole computational mechanism of the entire architecture. The core cross-attention operation (decoder queries attending to encoder representations via learned compatibility scores and weighted summation) is directly inherited, changing only the scoring function (additive to scaled dot-product) and adding multi-head parallelism. The Transformer's key innovations beyond Bahdanau are: (1) self-attention (within-sequence attention replacing recurrence), (2) multi-head attention (parallel attention subspaces), (3) positional encoding (compensating for loss of sequential processing), and (4) the resulting full parallelism and O(1) path length. Bahdanau's unique contributions (bidirectional RNN encoder, GRU decoder, additive attention scoring) are replaced in the Transformer, not extended. The relationship is EXT in the sense that the Transformer takes the attention idea and builds an entirely new architecture around it, achieving dramatic empirical improvements.
